newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian inflation under control - Finance official.
newsitem.headline: Indian inflation under control - Finance official.

text.p: India's inflation rate is well under control and the nation's central bank is carefully monitoring prices, a senior Finance Ministry official said.

Finance Secretary Montek Singh Ahluwalia said in a statement in Paris which was released in New Delhi on Wednesday that monetary and credit policy for 1997/98 (April-March) seeks to contain M3 growth within a target band of 15 to 15.5 percent.
Money supply growth as measured by M3 is currently running a little higher than projected because of the continued buoyancy of reserve inflows, Ahluwalia said.
"But inflation is well under control, and the Reserve Bank of India is carefully monitoring developments on a continuous basis," he said.
"Furthermore, there is the welcome sign of a downward trend in the rates of interest," he said.

"While inflation was on a downward trend in 1995/96, the rates of interest were slow to adjust and, in real terms, the rates of interest had become somewhat high creating problems for businesses as well as problems of adverse selection in the allocation of bank credit," he said.
"I am happy to report that the real interest rates have come down significantly since October 1996," he said.
Ahluwalia was speaking at the India Development Forum in Paris which ended on Wednesday.
